messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: comparing amose and lavaan results
parts:
On 04/06/2014 01:40 PM, muhammad faran wrote:
> thanx for quick answering
>
> Q1- actually im comparing all robust estimates for non-normal or
> outliers data so its very important to know me that those are
> comparable??? when applying on non-normal or outlier data???

I would recommend this book chapter:

Finney, SJ & DiStefano, C. (2006). Nonnormal and categorical data in
structural equation modeling. (Chapter 9 in Hancock & Mueller (eds).
Structural equation modeling: A second course)

For specific information about outliers, you can read:

Yuan, K. H., & Bentler, P. M. (1998). Structural equation modeling with
robust covariances. Sociological methodology, 28(1), 363-396.

Yuan, K. H., & Bentler, P. M. (2001). Effect of outliers on estimators
and tests in covariance structure analysis. British Journal of
Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 54(1), 161-175.

> Q-2 When im applying WLS as an estimator an error is occur .... i think
> the problem is weight matrix ... how we enter weight matrix here???
>
> > sem(semo, data = N85, estimator = "WLS")
> Error in lavaan::lavaan(model = semo, data = N85, estimator = "WLS",
> model.type = "sem", :
> object 'FLAT' not found
Something is wrong with 'semo'. This has nothing to do with the estimator.
> Q-3 when using estimator "DWLS" . are weights are variances???

The weight matrix (the 'W' in WLS) is the inverse of the asymptotic
variance matrix of the sample statistics (thresholds, polychorics). See
muthen (1984) for the theory.
> Q-4 are they WLSM, WLSMVS, WLSMV robust estimates for DWLS.?

estimator="WLSMV" implies:
1) estimator="DWLS"
2) se="robust"
3) test="scaled.shifted"

WLSMVS only affects the test to the 'old' mean and variance
Satterthwaite correction:

1) estimator="DWLS"
2) se="robust"
3) test="mean.var.adjusted"

WLSM only affects the test, using the mean-adjustment only (aka Satorra
Bentler)

1) estimator="DWLS"
2) se="robust"
3) test="satorra.bentler"

WLS implies:

1) estimator="WLS"
2) se="standard"
3) test="standard"

Yves
